blocks.text: Surrey condos and townhomes: 13 months of listings, sales and prices to October 2026

Over the 13 months from October 2025 to October 2026, listings of condos and townhomes in Surrey peaked at 1,565 in May 2026 and bottomed at 1,085 in December 2025. Sales were strongest in October 2025 with 194. The reported sale price moved from $580,000 to $547,500, a change of −5.6%.

items.t: Surrey townhomes are a city-wide search, not one neighbourhood: the City divides Surrey into six communities — Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey and Whalley — and townhouse stock sits in all six, heaviest where neighbourhood concept plans designated townhouse land.

The townhome belt a buyer actually tours runs along Fraser Highway through Fleetwood and Clayton, along 74 Avenue in West Clayton, and along 168 Street in Darts Hill and Grandview Heights in South Surrey — each cluster is named in a current City planning report below.

Surrey is in the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board (FVREB) area, not the Greater Vancouver board area, so a Surrey townhome search uses FVREB sub-areas such as Fleetwood Tynehead, Clayton and Grandview Heights.

The current Surrey townhome form is a strata cluster built under a townhouse or multiple-residential zone, not a row of freehold houses: a May 2026 City report describes a 45-unit townhouse development at 1928 168 Street rezoned from Acreage Residential (RA) to Multiple Residential 30 (RM-30).

Smaller infill clusters are the other Surrey pattern: 14 townhouse units at 10195 160 Street in Fleetwood, on a site rezoned from Urban Residential (R3) to Comprehensive Development (CD), and 12 units at 13054 112 Avenue near Scott Road, rezoned to Medium Density Townhouse Zone (MR2).

blocks.text: Surrey Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Surrey's 2026 zoning update renames the townhouse zones: the City's May 25, 2026 corporate report lists MR1 as Low Density Townhouse Zone and MR2 as Medium Density Townhouse Zone, alongside RM-10, RM-15 and RM-23 multiple-residential zones, in amendments to Surrey Zoning By-law, 1993, No. 12000.

Streamside setbacks can shrink a townhome site: the 10195 160 Street proposal needed a Development Permit for Hazardous Lands and Sensitive Ecosystems and a variance to streamside setbacks, because part of the Fleetwood site sits in a protected riparian corridor.

blocks.text: Surrey Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: A townhome pays the multiplex waste rate, not the detached rate alone: the City charges waste collection of $344.08 for 2026 to a single-family house, duplex or multiplex, collected with property taxes — a strata townhome's share flows through that billing structure.

Metered Surrey homes are billed for water and sewer every four months and sewer volume is charged at 88 percent of water supplied, with a 5 percent penalty on an unpaid metered balance after the due date — relevant in complexes where utilities are metered per unit rather than covered by strata fees.

A townhome built beside a creek may carry a conveyed green corridor: the 13054 112 Avenue project conveys about 0.12 acres (500 square metres) to the City as open space to preserve the Green Infrastructure Network corridor along the watercourse, land the strata does not own or maintain.

blocks.text: Surrey Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: 1928 168 Street (Darts Hill) — 45 townhouse units, rezoning from RA to RM-30 with a development permit; STATUS: planning report dated May 11, 2026 recommending public notification and first to third reading, read 2026-11-03.

18980 and 18990 74 Avenue (West Clayton) — 111 townhouse units, rezoning from RA to MR4 with an Official Community Plan amendment for the north portion; STATUS: planning report dated June 29, 2026, bylaw introduction recommended, read 2026-11-03.

5880 192 Street (Clayton) — 34 townhouse units, all three-bedroom plus den, rezoning from RA to RM-30 with an Official Community Plan density amendment from 37 to 59 units per hectare; STATUS: planning report dated May 11, 2026, read 2026-11-03.

18253 74 Avenue (West Clayton) — 32 townhouse units on a 6,723 square metre site east of 182 Street, rezoning from RA to RM-30 with a development variance permit; STATUS: additional planning comments report dated April 27, 2026, read 2026-11-03.

10195 160 Street (Fleetwood) — 14 townhouse units, rezoning from R3 to CD with hazardous-lands and sensitive-ecosystem development permits; STATUS: planning report dated May 11, 2026, read 2026-11-03.
The townhome-specific charge a buyer can verify is waste: $344.08 for 2026 for a single-family house, duplex or multiplex, collected with the property tax notice due July 2.

A secondary suite levy does not apply to a standard townhome unit: the City's suite charge is defined for a self-contained unit inside a detached, semi-detached or duplex house, so a townhome buyer should not budget the $1,275.71 suite utility levy unless the unit itself contains a separately levied suite, which the utility page does not describe for townhomes.

North Surrey townhomes near Scott Road use the R6 Scott Road RapidBus from Scott Road Station to Newton Exchange along Scott Road and 72 Avenue, and RapidBus routes run at least every 10 minutes at peak and every 15 minutes off-peak, 6 a.m. to midnight, on TransLink's project page.

The 12-unit project at 13054 112 Avenue is described by the City as close to both Gateway and Scott Road SkyTrain stations and about 150 metres outside the City Centre Plan boundary — the transit position for the Bridgeview-edge townhome cluster.

items.t: In a complex approved under a Comprehensive Development (CD) zone, the rules are the CD bylaw for that site, not the standard RM-30 zone — setbacks, amenity space and parking can all differ from the complex across the street, so the strata's Form B and the CD bylaw are the documents to read.

faq.q: Is a Surrey townhome strata or freehold?
faq.a: Most newer Surrey townhomes are strata, built as one project under a townhouse zone such as RM-30, MR2 or MR4 after a rezoning and a form-and-character development permit. The City reports above describe each cluster as a single development application — 45 units at 1928 168 Street, 111 units at 18980 74 Avenue — so buyers get strata bylaws, a depreciation report and common-property amenity space, not a freehold lot. Check the Form B for the specific complex.

faq.q: Why are so many Surrey townhomes in Clayton?
faq.a: Because the West Clayton Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) designated the land for cluster townhousing before it was built. The form is planned, not incidental.

faq.q: Which school does a Clayton or Fleetwood townhome feed into?
faq.a: The catchment is set by the exact address, not by the complex name. Surrey Schools (School District 36) states that a catchment school is determined by the address and the district's School Boundaries Map, and directs families to its School Locator tool before registering. Two complexes on the same street can split between schools, so run the unit's civic address through the locator before writing an offer that depends on a school.

faq.q: What amenity space should a newer Surrey townhome complex have?
faq.a: An older complex with no amenity building is not breaking a rule — it was approved under the standards of its day — but the comparison matters when fees are similar.
